summary.intent: Plan and execute Phase 69 of the CipherBox project ('FUSE and WinFsp — Rust Integration and Grant-Root Awareness'), porting the node/v3 model and grant-root-aware SDK-owned read chain from the TS stack to the Rust desktop stack (FUSE/WinFsp), then verify it via a real desktop-e2e run once the user flagged that root-key recovery wiring was required for a meaningful completion gate.
summary.outcome: Planned and executed 25 plans across repeated architectural re-scoping: the full core/sdk node/v3 foundation, the atomic FUSE cutover (done via an 11-slice grind), JournalOp reshape, grant-scoped delete/rename, recycle-bin and vault-creation migrations, legacy-type deletion (D-04 complete), and a 5-plan vault-blob-v3 root-key recovery port replacing a placeholder '^0xA5' key-bridge — all merged and workspace-green. Only 69-14 (WinFsp/Windows, autonomous:false) remains, deferred to the user's Windows machine; live desktop-e2e had not yet been run at transcript end.

repo: GSD commit helper (`gsd-tools.cjs`) reports 'commit_failed' as a false negative even when the commit lands cleanly — always verify via `git log --oneline -1`, never retry the commit.

Worktree-isolated executors sometimes mis-report `<worktree_metadata>` `expected_base` as their own last docs commit instead of the true fork point — always verify via `git merge-base <branch> HEAD` before recording/merging.

`cargo fmt` invoked at the crate root (e.g. via `rustfmt lib.rs` following `mod` declarations) reformats the entire module tree; executors must scope-check diffs and revert out-of-scope reformatted files before committing.
CI workflow is actually named 'Desktop E2E Tests', not 'CI E2E Tests' as ROADMAP/CONTEXT word it — `gh workflow run "CI E2E Tests"` would 404.
`ApiNodeFetcher` in crates/sdk is a lifetime-bound borrow adapter with no `::new` constructor — must be constructed inline at each call site, not stored as a struct field.

`RotationHighWater<S>` is not `Clone` by default; deriving Clone is safe since its `JsonSidecarFloorStore` only holds a `PathBuf` and does read-modify-write on disk (a clone shares the same durable floor).

Desktop worktrees often lack `node_modules`, causing the husky pre-commit `lint-staged` hook to fail on the first commit — either run `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` or use `--no-verify` for pure-Rust changes it wouldn't touch anyway.

The web side (packages/core, sdk-core) had already shipped the real node/v3 vault-key model (vault blob v3, two independent random root keys) in #578/#587/#588 — the Rust desktop was still silently on the legacy v2 single-key blob with a fabricated '^0xA5' bridge, making web-created and desktop-created vaults mutually unreadable.

A frozen cross-language KAT vector (`tests/vectors/vault-v3-blob.json`) already existed for the vault-blob-v3 format, waiting for a Rust port — evidence the TS/Rust parity process front-loads test vectors before implementation lands on both sides.

Legacy folder-model types (`FolderMetadata`, `FilePointer`, `FolderEntry`, etc.) were NOT dead code as originally assumed — they were load-bearing for the recycle-bin subsystem, vault-export/restore blobs (ECIES keepers), and vault-creation, none of which were in the original phase scope.

code.finding: JournalOp originally cited as the cross-crate 'weld' blocking a clean FUSE cutover; later verified as stale/nonexistent — the actual parent_metadata:FolderMetadata field lived in fuse-side MkdirJournalResult, not the cross-crate JournalOp, invalidating that landmine framing in the re-scoped plan.

list_folder_owned is the gated write-plane tree-materialization entrypoint (69-17), recovering per-node {read_key, write_key, ipns_private_key} through the same SC#6 gate as list_folder; resolve_published_node stays pub(crate).
Vault blob v3 format is 0x03 | u16_BE(readLen) | ECIES(rootReadKey) | u16_BE(writeLen) | ECIES(rootWriteKey), envelope-only (no crypto in the codec); v2 codec preserved unmodified alongside it.
Root read/write keys were bridged from the legacy root_folder_key via '^0xA5' pending real node/v3 root-key recovery — later replaced in 69-24 by real recovered KeyState.root_read_key/root_write_key.

InodeKind is a read-WRITE vault-owner state (stores ipns_private_key to sign IPNS records plus folder_key/write_key), not a read-only client like the web 68.2 mirror — this was the deepest architectural gap blocking the atomic FUSE flip until 69-17 delivered owned key materialization.

workflow: For a large atomic architectural cutover that repeatedly stalls on session/usage limits, chunk it into a bounded multi-slice grind on a single shared branch (each slice commits even while RED), with a committed runbook capturing the authoritative target shape and carry-forward facts between slices so the grind survives interruption.

When an sdk-green-but-workspace-red foundation plan and its dependent consumer plan are tightly coupled, dispatch the consumer executor to continue directly on the foundation plan's branch (non-isolated, via git -C + absolute paths) rather than merging the red state, so the combined unit merges as one workspace-green commit.

When a worktree executor halts with an architectural blocker, independently re-verify its key grep/scope claims against the live tree before accepting or escalating to the user — sub-agent reports can be accurate but should not be relayed uncritically.

A 'canary' pattern (execute one plan synchronously worktree-isolated before fanning out the rest of a wave in parallel) is a cheap way to validate the full executor→worktree→merge→build pipeline before committing unattended parallel dispatch.
When re-scoping mid-execution, prefer delegating research+planning to fresh sub-agents (role separation) even under `--auto`, rather than the orchestrator authoring plans inline.

friction: The gsd-planner agent crashed mid-run (API error, connection closed) after writing 13 of 14 plans, requiring filesystem-fallback recovery and a fresh single-plan planner dispatch.
The commit helper's persistent 'commit_failed' false negative required manual git log verification after nearly every commit throughout the session.

Two separate agent deaths from account/session usage limits (mid-exploration on 69-09's first retry, and mid-slice on 69-16) required backing off and resuming rather than treating them as architectural blockers.

The FUSE cutover (69-09) hit three successive, progressively deeper architectural blockers during execution — read/write coupling wider than scoped, missing Node write-plane emit API + read adapter, and missing read-write-owner key-materialization infrastructure — each requiring a research→plan→user-approval cycle before execution could resume.

Even after the atomic flip landed, 69-10's 'delete all legacy types' premise turned out to be invalid because the recycle-bin, vault-export, and vault-creation subsystems still depended on the legacy types, forcing yet another expansion (69-19, 69-20) before 69-10 could run.

After the phase was reported 'complete' at 19/20 plans, the user's review surfaced that the desktop root-key recovery was still a placeholder bridge, meaning the deferred desktop-e2e gate would have been meaningless — requiring a whole additional 5-plan expansion (69-21–69-25) discovered via fresh investigation.
cargo fmt-on-crate-root repeatedly over-reformatted unrelated files across multiple executor runs, requiring manual `git checkout --` reverts to keep diffs scoped.
open_items: 69-14 (WinFsp/Windows integration, autonomous:false, requirements:[TEST-03]) is not yet executed — deferred to the user's Windows machine as the natural hand-off point.

Live desktop-e2e (native local stack: Postgres/api/Kubo/Redis/mock-ipns-routing + FUSE-T, via --dev-key/--test-login) had not yet been run at transcript end — this is the completion gate the user explicitly required before marking the phase complete.

ROT-07 live-wiring gap: shared-scope-exit deletes/renames on Unix currently fail closed (EIO) because no production RotationDeps implementor exists yet; private deletes are fully correct and secure-by-default.
File versioning is not reconstructed on write in the node/v3 model (InodeKind dropped `versions`; NodeContent.versions is written as empty) — flagged as a regression to verify at E2E.
Orphaned parent-CID pins are no longer unpinned on republish since metadata_cache no longer surfaces the old CID — GC-able, not correctness-critical, but unresolved.

The `--features winfsp` build is expected-RED on macOS (windows-crate dependency issues); Windows CI (`cargo-windows` job) is the only authoritative gate for the platform/windows/* edits made best-effort during the grind.
